revision_history.change_rationale: Refined connection routing, official resources and semantic micro-motion after prior visual rejection.
Added semantic legend and synchronized Engineering labels to routed SVG paths.
Added generic connection-centric Engineering behavior, but the active KAYAS T02 NORMALIZED_HINTS service-domain model prevented the expected spine/leaf engineering composition.
Separated Presentation T02 from a device-role Engineering profile so the 210-cabinet service-domain story could coexist with evidence-safe network engineering composition.

User confirmed the v1a9 renderer loaded but still looked like grouped colored cards rather than the approved engineering mockup. Added a member-decomposed, connection-first T02 renderer: QTY-based network/security/OOB groups are visually expanded into member placeholders, spine-to-leaf fabric is shown only as explicitly labelled illustrative design intent, and canonical graph data remains unchanged.

observations: The v1a9 renderer was confirmed loaded by the visible T02 NETWORK ENGINEERING TOPOLOGY toolbar.
Functional layers and role colors were readable, but QTY 2 / QTY 4 network objects remained visually grouped inside single object cards.
The resulting composition still read as layered infrastructure cards rather than a classic engineer-readable topology with separate spine, leaf, firewall, interconnect and OOB member nodes.
Connection labels remained visually dominant in several areas and the management plane still behaved more like a sidebar than a network topology domain.
No evidence-discipline violation was observed; the rejection was visual/engineering readability rather than semantic correctness.

iteration_4e_changes: Added v1a10 member-decomposed T02 Engineering renderer and stylesheet as a new overlay; prior renderers remain preserved for rollback until visual acceptance.
Network/security/OOB canonical objects with quantity up to four are decomposed into quantity-derived visual member placeholders rather than remaining single pair/group cards.
Visual Member 1 / Visual Member 2 labels are explicitly non-canonical placeholders derived only from the quantity field; they do not create device identities or mutate objects.json.
Single-quantity management objects remain visually recognizable by their actual object display name rather than being presented as a synthetic pair member.
CAS compute hosts and All-Flash storage nodes remain aggregated endpoint groups to control visual density; no ten-host or six-node physical fanout is invented.
Spine-to-leaf design intent is rendered as an illustrative multi-line fabric pattern only when the existing AINT-005 Spine-to-Leaf Fabric presentation intent is present.
The illustrative fabric is explicitly labelled MEMBER MAPPING UNCONFIRMED and uses a separate dotted visual grammar so it cannot be mistaken for evidenced physical links.
Security chain, external ingress, security handoff, interconnect-to-fabric, compute access, storage access and storage data path remain dashed design-intent paths.
OOB-to-fabric, fabric control and fabric telemetry paths use a separate management/OOB grammar and filter.
No ring, HA, IRF, MLAG, M-LAG, EVPN, VXLAN, A/B naming, ports, optics, speeds or confirmed member-to-member physical mapping was added.
The object drawer states that member placeholders are quantity-derived only and that actual member name, A/B, HA, ports, speeds and optics remain OPEN-CONFIRMATION REQUIRED.
The KAYAS preview loads v1a10 with cache revision v1a10b; production viewer remains untouched.

static_checks.check: Live browser visual/runtime acceptance for Iteration 4E
static_checks.method: Requires user browser evidence after cache-busted refresh

manual_acceptance_required: Open KAYAS T02 in ENGINEERING mode using a fresh/cache-busted URL.

Perimeter Firewall, ADC, Egress Firewall, Legacy Interconnect, Spine, Leaf, Storage Switch and OOB quantity groups must be visibly decomposed into separate member placeholders rather than one large pair/group card.
Spine and Leaf must read as separate engineering nodes and the illustrative spine-to-leaf cross-fabric must be visible without being presented as canonical or physical evidence.
The in-canvas fabric note must state that member mapping is unconfirmed.
Compute and storage endpoint groups must remain aggregated and readable rather than exploding into ten/six unsupported physical nodes.
Management/OOB paths must be independently filterable and use a distinct visual grammar.
Selecting a quantity-derived member placeholder must open the drawer and explicitly state that the member identity is not canonical.
Design paths Off must hide all dashed/dotted design and illustrative paths.
No ring, HA/peer protocol, A/B names, EVPN/VXLAN, port, link speed or optic may appear without explicit evidence.
T03 must remain unchanged and continue to show zero evidenced physical connectivity.
KAYAS and Haven production viewers must remain unchanged.
notes: Iteration 4E is a deliberate visual decomposition layer, not a canonical device-instance generator. Quantity-derived member placeholders exist only to make the engineering topology read like a network diagram while preserving DCTS evidence discipline. Explicit user browser acceptance remains mandatory before any production promotion.
